title: BIMAX: A Bitwise In-Memory Accelerator Using 6T-SRAM Structure
problem: SRAM-based in-memory computing has limited operations and unreliable accuracy due to environmental noise and process variations.
motivation: In-memory computing in SRAM is fundamentally fast but limited in functionality and robustness; broader operation support with noise resilience enables wider applicability.
method: BIMAX uses novel imbalanced differential sense amplifier design to perform parallel bitwise operations (AND, OR, NOT, XOR, NAND, NXOR) and row-copy on multiple 6T-SRAM cells simultaneously, with result write-back capability.
key_novelty: Imbalanced differential sense amplifier architecture enabling reliable bitwise operations with noise robustness in standard 6T-SRAM.
contributions: 52.7% lower energy dissipation vs state-of-the-art IMC
5.4× improved noise robustness against environmental variations
